name: Euler Finance: copied exploit contract executes the DAI-market exploit first, proceeds routed to the hacker by a hard-coded destination
race_type_reason: The copier deployed a byte-near-identical copy of the attacker's exploit contract one block after the attacker's deploy (4 x 20-byte address swaps) and used its DAI-market entry point at the top of block 16817996, 17 blocks before the attacker's first (failed) call. It is the attacker's own on-chain setup being used before the attacker's call, not a calldata replay.
one_liner: A fresh EOA copied the Euler attacker's exploit contract one block after its deploy, swapping only the owner address, and ran its DAI-market entry point at block 16817996 position 0: 8,877,507 DAI out of Euler. Funds went to the attacker's hard-coded wallet; the copier captured nothing.

attack_txs.role: deploy the exploit contract 0x036cec1a (3 gwei tip)
attacker's first call (WETH-market entry 0xa91864d4); out of gas in the Aave delegatecall; 17 blocks after the copier's DAI-market exploit
attacker's first successful call (WETH market, 20,895 WETH flash loan)

bots_other.label: anon searcher (copier)
bots_other.role: deploy of the copy contract 0xebc29199c817dc47ba12e3f86102564d640cbf99 (creation calldata identical to the attacker's except 4 x 20 bytes), one block after the attacker's deploy; tip 37.1 gwei

bots_other.label: anon searcher (copier)
bots_other.role: second byte-identical copy deployed in the same block as the attacker's first failed call; never successfully called (calls by other addresses reverted). A causal link to the attacker's out-of-gas failure is not shown.

mempool_note: In-block evidence only: March 2023 is before the mempool-dumpster archive (starts 2023-08-07). It is unknown whether the copier saw the attacker's deploy in the public mempool or only after block 16817993 landed, 12 s before the copy deploy was included.

trigger.note: No mempool first-seen exists (pre-archive). Reference event is the attacker's deploy tx 0x50dc9c91 in block 16817993 (2023-03-13T08:50:23Z).

attacker_block_note: Block of the attacker's FIRST call to its own contract (tx 0xa476fad7, index 44, WETH-market entry, out of gas); its first success was block 16818024 (tx 0x47ac3527). This is 17 blocks AFTER the copier's DAI-market exploit; the attacker never called the DAI entry point. The race is the whole deployed contract, so attacker_reference is the deploy.

loot.gross_loot_method: not converted: the proceeds are DAI and no ETH/DAI price is saved for this block; not invented

captured_native.desc: net DAI left in the copy contract 0xebc29199c817dc47ba12e3f86102564d640cbf99: 38,904,507.35 DAI from Euler plus 30,000,000 DAI Aave flash loan minus 30,000,000 DAI the copy sent into Euler minus 30,027,000 DAI repaid; later sent by the copy's withdraw() to the attacker's hard-coded wallet 0xb66cd966670d962c227b3eaba30a872dbfb995db

loot.captured_usd_source: DAI at par (stablecoin), amount from the callTracer trace of tx 0xc310a0af; same figure as incident.json routed_to_hacker_usd (8,877,507). This went to the hacker's wallet, not to the copier.
loot.loot_note: bot_net_eth is 0: the copier captured nothing. The DAI sat in its copy until the copier itself called withdraw() (tx 0xdae809e4, block 16818823), which sent all 8,877,507.35 DAI to the wallet baked into the creation code (0xb66cd966670d962c227b3eaba30a872dbfb995db, the attacker's wallet). Costs are NOT netted: the attack tx cost 0.1108 ETH of gas (0.0739 ETH tip + base fee), about 0.61 ETH across all the copier's txs per incident.json. Euler's net DAI-market loss in this tx was 8,904,507.35 DAI (Euler paid out 38,904,507.35 DAI and received 30,000,000 DAI); the whole Euler hack is about $197M (PeckShield figure, not re-verified here). No coinbase transfer: the tip (0.0739 ETH) is 78% of the 0.09425 ETH winning bid, so position 0 came from the public gas-price auction, not a bundle. No builder refund seen.

fate.returned_desc: Nothing reached Euler from this row. The copier's contract can only pay the address hard-coded in its bytecode, so its withdraw() (block 16818823, about 2 h 47 min after the exploit) sent all 8,877,507.35 DAI to the attacker's wallet. The copier's on-chain message (tx 0x44b559c8, block 16818973) says it tried to return the money and 'unfortunately it sent the money to the hacker's address'. Any later return by the Euler hacker to Euler is outside this row and not covered by our saved files.
fate.public_statement: On-chain message from the copier EOA to itself (tx 0x44b559c8): Hi I am the owner of a MEV bot that has accidentally frontrun the first tx of the hacker. It tried to frontrun the second tx but failed and only the contract has been created. I tried to return the money but the contract can only send to an address already in bytecode. Unfotunately it sent the money to the hacker's address. I tried my best and I am very sorry for anyone who lost money.
fate.return_status_rule: returned = everything went back to the victim side except a bounty the victim agreed to or offered; partial = some came back, otherwise; none = known zero within the documented search window; unknown = unresolved

rawref_gaps.why: proceeds are DAI; no saved ETH price for the block; left null
Tornado funding per incident.json (tx 0x4ec892aa, block 16817962) taken from the incident, not re-opened here

discrepancies: attacker_block (16818013) is AFTER the bot block (16817996): the attacker's first call came 17 blocks later, so blocks_ahead from attacker_block would be negative. The meaningful reference is the attacker's deploy (16817993), which the bot's deploy copy followed by one block and the bot's exploit by three.

Strictly the copier did not replay an attacker tx: it re-deployed the attacker's contract with its own owner constant and called an entry point (0x863df8af, DAI) the attacker never called. Whether the attacker would have used that entry point is unknown.
evidence_notes: Creation calldata of the copier's deploy (tx 0x725db76c, block 16817994) and the attacker's deploy (tx 0x50dc9c91, block 16817993) is 17,115 bytes each and differs in exactly 80 bytes = four 20-byte occurrences of the attacker EOA 0xb2698c2d replaced by 0x5f259d0b at offsets [353, 1454, 7355, 15144]; the hard-coded 0xb66cd966 is in both (recomputed from site/raw/rpc/tx_*.json; incidents/euler-copybot-2023/bytecode_diff.json). Both deploys used exactly 4,181,203 gas.

Block 16817996 position 0: tx 0xc310a0af calls the copy's entry 0x863df8af: Aave V2 flash loan 30,000,000 DAI, 38,904,507.35 DAI out of Euler, 30,027,000 DAI repaid, 8,877,507.35 DAI left in the copy (trace in site/raw/rpc/trace_tx_0xc310a0af....json).

The attacker's first call to its own contract used the WETH entry 0xa91864d4 in block 16818013 and ran out of gas; its first success was block 16818024. It never called the DAI entry point 0x863df8af, which exists in its identical bytecode.
Copier's withdraw() (tx 0xdae809e4, block 16818823) transfers 8,877,507.35 DAI to 0xb66cd966, the address hard-coded in both contracts; calls to the copies by other EOAs reverted (incident.json).

Ordering: tip 37.9 gwei vs 17.5 gwei for index 1, no coinbase payment; winning builder Flashbots, 0.09425 ETH. Owner claim 'MEV bot' rests only on the copier's own on-chain message; on-chain it is a fresh single-purpose EOA.
caveat: The copier may be the attacker’s own second account: it was a fresh single-purpose EOA, kept the attacker’s cash-out wallet and captured nothing. Its own on-chain message is the only claim that it was a bot.
